newsitem.title: TAIWAN: FORECAST - Taiwan 1997 corn imports seen tumbling.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Taiwan 1997 corn imports seen tumbling.

text.p: Grain traders said on Tuesday they expected Taiwan's 1997 corn imports to fall significantly from 1996 because of an outbreak of foot and mouth disease that has sharply reduced demand for animal feed.

In a Reuters Poll conducted on Tuesday, corn buyers and traders from six key grain firms all forecast that imports would fall sharply from 1996, when Taiwan bought about 6.5 million tonnes of corn, according to private estimates.
Forecasts for 1997 imports ranged from just 4.9 million tonnes to as high as 5.8 million tonnes and averaged about five million tonnes.
Forecasts for 1997 Taiwan corn imports (in millions of tonnes):
Several major international grain trading companies declined to participate in the Reuters Poll, saying such information could affect hypersensitive corn prices and futures.

The U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) on Monday forecast that Taiwan would import 5.83 million tonnes of U.S. corn in the 1996/97 marketing year, a sharp downward revision from its earlier estimate of 6.33 million.

Experts said the USDA forecast was higher than the Taiwan traders' estimates because it uses a September to August marketing year and includes more months before the March 20 outbreak of hog foot and mouth disease in Taiwan.
"The USDA number is mostly based on months that were not affected by the hog disease," Marubeni Heartland Food Group director Hubert Chen told Reuters by telephone.

The deadly and highly contagious airborne foot and mouth virus has been detected on 3,422 of Taiwan's 25,000 hog farms, with officials projecting that 2.86 million of the island's 14 million pigs would have to be destroyed.
Taiwan was the third largest buyer of U.S. corn in 1996.
